title: MACH Factory Event v3 (normalised view)
description: One event of the Control Tower's normalised history, as the observer serves it to a client. Version 3 is a VIEW: nothing writes it to .factory/. It is produced by the observer from five sources that stay as they are on disk: the intake log (factory-event v2, unchanged), each cell's lifecycle.jsonl, each execution's started.json and result.json, runs.jsonl, and each execution's stream.jsonl. Every field here is browser-safe by construction; fields that never leave the observer are listed in M6_1_EVENT_CONTRACT.md section 9. This schema is strict for producers (conformance tests); consumers must ignore unknown fields and kinds within version 3. Design: docs/mach-next/M6_1_EVENT_CONTRACT.md.

schema_revision.description: Additive revisions within version 3. Consumers ignore fields and kinds they do not know. Revision 1: execution.usage gains cost_complete and cost_incomplete_reasons. Revision 2: history.gap gains class and history_lost (and the reasons unexpected-shape and evicted); origin gains runtime_state on execution-stream events. Revision 3: execution.started gains source_commit, provenance (the snapshot the supervisor took at start, or null) and provenance_reason.

id.description: Deterministic from source and source sequence; rebuilding the index gives the same id. See M6_1_EVENT_CONTRACT.md section 5.

pos.description: Delivery position in this observer index epoch. The cursor. Not the history order.

key.description: The source partition: i:<gen>, c:<ticket>:<gen>, x:<execution_id>, r:<gen>, s:<execution_id>, o.

seq.description: Durable per-source sequence: v2 seq, lifecycle seq, runs.jsonl line, stream.jsonl line, 1/2 for started/result. Null for observer events.

part.description: Sub-index when one source record yields several events (a message with several tool calls).

script.description: For station writers: the script, e.g. build.py.

runtime_state.description: Revision 2. Only on an event read from an execution stream: the state of the Claude Code runtime that wrote it, when the record was read. proven: a version the observer's fixtures come from; compatible-unproven: another version whose records have all matched the known shapes; incompatible: records of this stream were refused for their shape (this one matched); unknown: no init record read yet. Absent on every other event.

order_ms.description: Unix ms used to place the event in history; never earlier than the previous event of the same source.

order.description: Deterministic total history order: order_ms, source rank, source key, seq, part.

cell_instance.description: The generation of the ticket's cell: first 8 hex of the SHA-256 of the first line of its lifecycle.jsonl.

visit_id.description: <ticket>/<station>#<n>; with ~<k> after the ticket for a cell's k-th incarnation, k >= 2.

round.description: Judging round, 1 to 3 (the lifecycle record's round; older v1 files call it attempt).

attempt.description: The supervisor's execution attempt for the ticket at its current step (work.claimed, execution.failed). Not the judging round.

agent_id.description: <execution_id>/<workflow agentId (a + 16 hex)>, <execution_id>/<Agent-tool agent_id>, or <execution_id>/main. Opaque: never parsed by views.

entities.description: Every entity this event touches, as the Control Tower's kind:id refs. Computed by the observer; views never derive them.

parent.description: The enclosing span's entity (a tool call's agent, an agent's parent agent or visit, a visit's execution when recorded).

cause.description: Only when a writer recorded the link (recorded) or both records carry the same identifier (identity). Never from temporal adjacency.

unknown.description: Fields that apply to this event but are not known (as opposed to null meaning not applicable).

inferred.description: Fields the observer filled by inference, with the rule. cause is never inferred.

provenance.description: How the event came to be. Required for reconstructed events (basis event ids, the rule, the files read). On any other event it is null, except {basis: [], rule: 'backfill', files: []} when the event was read during catch-up (contract 6.5).

late.description: Read live and delivered after the observer had already delivered an event that sorts after it in history order. Never true for backfill (history read while catching a source up with what was written before the observer started, or after an index rebuild); backfill carries provenance rule 'backfill' instead. Contract section 6.5.

withheld.description: How many source fields the allow-list or redaction dropped from this event.

source_commit.description: Revision 3. The intake log's product source commit on this event.

provenance_reason.description: Revision 3. Why provenance is null: not-recorded (none at start: every execution before M6.5), capture-failed (the supervisor could not take it; the execution ran as usual), not-understood (another snapshot schema, or a null snapshot with a reason this observer does not know). Null when provenance is present.

provenance.description: Revision 3. The snapshot the supervisor took once, at start (skills/run/scripts/provenance.py). Digests, versions, identifiers, numbers and booleans only.

models.description: A name that is not a plain identifier is sha256:<digest>.

counts.description: Integer and boolean facts the station recorded (tasks, items, errors, problems). Never strings.
Integer and boolean facts the station recorded (tasks, items, errors, problems). Never strings.

app_type.description: Revision 2. The app type the plan station recorded on its exit (cell.json app_type); absent on other exits.

risk.description: Revision 2. The risk tier the plan station recorded on its exit; absent on other exits.

gate.description: The station's own gate name, e.g. build.start, build.red, build.finish, verify.verdict, review.tally, merge.land, round-limit.

counts.description: Integer and boolean facts the station recorded (tasks, items, errors, problems). Never strings.

cost_complete.description: Revision 1. False when the reported spend may be lower than what was spent: a budget stop, or a killed workflow's agents still running when it was killed. Optional so revision-0 events still validate; the observer always writes it.

cost_incomplete_reasons.description: Revision 1. Why cost_complete is false; empty when it is true.

class.description: Revision 2. What the gap means: not-received (bytes missing: missing-seq, truncated, rewritten), unparsable-line (received, unreadable), unknown-type (received and well formed, not interpreted: unknown-type, unexpected-shape, no-timestamps), state-mismatch (records probably missing), evicted (no longer held), source-unreadable (unreadable), conflict (two differing copies; the first is kept).

history_lost.description: Revision 2. True when the gap loses history (not-received, unparsable-line, state-mismatch, evicted, source-unreadable); false for unknown-type and conflict, whose records were received.
